title: Attention tile coherence regression from async scheduler interleaving
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: After landing an aggressive attention-tile swapping optimization and an asynchronous prefill/decode interleaving scheduler, we are seeing correctness regressions manifesting as small-but-systematic numerical drift in logits and intermittent corruption of attention tile contents leading to decoding anomalies (repeated tokens, collapse to EOS, or token hallucinations). The bug appears at high concurrency and with mixed-precision kernels enabled.

Context: The new tile-swap path moves attention 'tiles' (packed head/seq ranges) between worker queues to improve cache locality and kernel utilization. The scheduler was changed to interleave prefill and decode work to improve end-to-end tail latency. Those two changes together reduce deterministic ordering of attention accumulation and expose a race where an old tile buffer is observed by a decode kernel while a prefill update is still streaming new KV data into that buffer. In some cases floating-point accumulation order changes cause measurable drift; in rarer cases a pointer aliasing/race causes partial overwrite and corrupted tile state.

Why this is urgent: A/B tests show a small but measurable reduction in generation quality for a subset of traffic (high concurrency, long contexts). This affects customer-facing hosted endpoints and Dedicated pools with mixed-precision enabled. We need a mitigation for the release window and a correctness fix for the runtime.
steps_to_reproduce: Run mixed-precision runtime with tile-swap enabled and async interleaving scheduler flag on
Use a long-context LLM (>= 4k tokens) and high concurrency (>= 48 concurrent requests)
Send a mix of prefill-heavy and single-token-decode traffic to force interleaving
Collect logs with --trace-tiles and enable numeric-diff mode comparing fp32 reference path
Observe occasional large per-token logit delta (>1e-2) or repeated token emission in output
investigation_notes: 2026-02-18: Initial triage by @Sofia — reproduced locally in stress harness at 64 workers. Noticed drift correlates with changed accumulation order in tiled softmax kernel.
2026-02-20: Added tile version stamping to trace when buffers are recycled; observed cases where decode kernel reads tile version X while prefill increments to X+1 mid-execution.
2026-02-25: Memory model analysis shows lack of a release/acquire fence around tile handoff in the scheduler; ordering relied on implicit CPU barriers that don't hold across worker pools.
2026-03-02: Replicated pointer-alias race where tiled buffer is freed back to pool and reallocated for a different request before decode finishes using it (rare): use-after-write symptoms.

2026-03-08: Floating-point repro with deterministic accumulators: when accumulation order changes (different tile ordering) we see stable but non-negligible logit drift (max 1e-3 to 5e-2 depending on layer). Not random noise — systematic across runs with same interleaving.
2026-03-10: Stress run with kernel-level mutex around tile accesses eliminated corruption but introduced 15% p99 latency regression and contention.
mitigation: Hotfix 1 (short-term): Roll back tile-swap optimization behind feature flag for hosted rollout and Dedicated autopools; revert scheduler interleaving flag to conservative mode for mixed-precision pools.
Hotfix 2 (medium): Add tile-version + read-barrier: decode kernels check tile version before using and retry via copy-on-read when mismatch detected (works but extra copy cost).
Hotfix 3 (safety): Introduce lightweight per-tile state machine with handoff semantics (state: Owned -> HandingOff -> InUse). Use atomic state transitions to avoid reuse races.
proposed_fix: Primary: update scheduler handoff to use atomic publish (release) on tile buffer and acquire in consumer kernel; ensure device-host sync where necessary and add explicit memory_barrier() after prefill completes writes.
Secondary: change tile allocator to bump-pointer with epoch-based reclamation per worker group to avoid immediate reuse while decode may still hold foggy references.
Numeric stability: adjust accumulation order to prefer higher-magnitude-first accumulation in mixed-precision kernels and add optional compensated summation in critical layers.
Perf compromise: introduce per-request 'deterministic' bit to bypass tile-swapping for requests with eval/quality-sensitive flags while letting low-priority traffic use swapped paths.
tests_and_metrics: Set up nightly numeric-diff job comparing runtime-1.24 against a fp32 deterministic baseline across 500 prompt seeds; track per-token KL divergence and top-1 token disagreement rate.
Add stress harness test that runs 10k mixed traffic requests with random interleaving and asserts no tile-version mismatches and zero-use-after-free occurrences.
Perf regression dashboard: p50/p95/p99 for generation latency and throughput under tile-swap on/off; track cost delta from copy-on-read mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: No reproducible corruption (use-after-write) in stress harness after fixes
Per-token KL drift reduced to <1e-4 against fp32 baseline for representative workloads
Rollout path: ability to enable tiled swap on 100% low-priority traffic while keeping deterministic path for sensitive traffic
No >5% regression in p99 latency after final mitigation in Dedicated pools
action_log: 2026-02-19: Alert to SRE and QA — flagged as P0 due to customer-impact signal from nightly evaluations.
2026-02-22: QA created reproducer harness and assigned to Marcus for deeper kernel traces.
2026-03-03: Team demoed a failing trace that shows tile-version mismatch; agreed on atomic handoff design as target fix.
2026-03-11: SRE approved targeted rollback plan for hosted region eu-west-1 and Dedicated autopool testbeds.
2026-03-12: Begin rollout of feature-flag rollback to 30% traffic as containment while patch PR is prepared.
next_steps: Finalize atomic handoff PR and run unit tests for memory model assertions (owner/publishing semantics)
Implement epoch-based allocator change and add unit tests to prevent immediate reclamation
Benchmark copy-on-read approach to understand worst-case cost and evaluate if it's an acceptable short-term mitigation
Coordinate with QA to add nightly numeric-diff and stress harness to CI gating for runtime-1.24 branch
Prepare customer communication for Dedicated customers outlining the temporary rollback and when correctness-fix will be available
